beats.acting: Agnes turns her attention from the hawk to acknowledge the unfamiliar man with measured courtesy.
Agnes's greeting gives way to direct curiosity as she studies why he has come to Hewlands.
Being recognized as the Latin tutor makes Will more self-conscious under Agnes's scrutiny.
Will's hesitation exposes his uncertainty, and he briefly drops his gaze while searching for an answer.
Agnes lightly teases him to make clear that her question is harmless while still watching his reaction.
Will re-engages with Agnes after his moment of avoidance and tries to explain himself.
The repeated hesitation makes Will's discomfort more visible as he struggles to frame an acceptable excuse.
Will searches inwardly for a plausible explanation before continuing.
Mentioning the bird gives Will safer ground, and his attention settles on the hawk.
Agnes follows his reference to the bird, briefly checking that he has noticed the hawk.
Agnes corrects him with quiet confidence, claiming the distinction without hostility.
The correction catches Will off guard, and he focuses on the hawk as he absorbs it.
